highlights.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
highlights.summary: Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that's designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users.
body: Imagine an endless feed of AI slop in which you are the main character of every story.

First spotted by Patentlyze, the patent — which was filed last May and published last week — describes how My Channel would use a person’s demographic data and viewing history to create its own prompts that would then be fed into an LLM to help generate AI videos tailored to that person’s specific interests. In addition to factoring in what kinds of videos a user tends to watch, the system would capture contextual data from their device like IP addresses, GPS locations, and specific details about the user’s age. My Channel could also base its prompts on current news like sports scores and things happening on social media, and all of the video generation would take place on Google’s servers.

highlights.title: England's All Blacks Tests 'World Cup practice' | 'Ireland still not contenders'
highlights.summary: Head coaches Steve Borthwick of England, Andy Farrell of Ireland and Dave Rennie of New Zealand speak to media ahead of the final weekend of the inaugural Nations Championship.
body: England, having come into the tournament under a cloud of pressure following the worst Six Nations display in their history earlier this year (four losses, fifth place), have stormed to victories over Australia, Japan and New Zealand this month.

Last week, Borthwick's side secured a record 25-point victory over the All Blacks at Allianz Stadium. With England finishing second behind France in the northern hemisphere standings and New Zealand runners-up to South Africa in the southern hemisphere table, the two sides are now set for an immediate rematch.
England face the All Blacks again at Twickenham on Saturday, with Borthwick viewing the latest clash as valuable preparation for the Rugby World Cup in Australia in 10 months' time.
"The nature of this tournament, it's a new tournament, is the understanding that international games have that level of jeopardy," Borthwick told the media on Wednesday.

highlights.title: 10 Classic Books Worth Reading Over and Over
highlights.summary: Most of us treat classic literature like a checklist to conquer in high school or college and then never touch those books again. You power through the plot, underline a few quotes for a term paper, and move on to whatever else is new.
body: When you reread classic literature, everything changes: you stop rushing toward the finale and focus instead on how the author pulled it all off. Whether they reshape your perspective as you age or hide their best clues in plain sight, these 10 books reward you on every return trip.

Dostoevsky borrows the mechanics of a detective novel as he weaves Raskolnikov’s psychological fallout into the overriding mystery, setting aside the familiar detective-versus-killer plot to peer into the killer’s mind​​​​​​​. When you aren't racing through its pages to see whether Raskolnikov gets caught by the investigator Porfiry Petrovich, you savor the cat-and-mouse mind games between them. Every feverish rationalization and defensive outburst reads like a man slowly building his own prison cell.

highlights.title: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor dies aged 65
highlights.summary: The musician, who co-wrote some of the band's biggest hits, had been treated for prostate cancer.
body: Andy Taylor, the guitarist for the pop group Duran Duran, has died at the age of 65.
Born in Tynemouth, he co-wrote some of the group's biggest hits, including Save A Prayer, Rio and Girls On Film; and also worked with artists like Robert Palmer, Rod Stewart and Belinda Carlisle.
In a statement, his bandmates said Taylor had fought "a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer" and "passed away peacefully at home, surrounded by his family, on Monday 23 November".
His wife, Tracey, said the musician "was the rock of our family", adding: "We will miss him every single day".

highlights.title: I tried leaving all my money to my sister. She said no – and forced me to think about who really needs it
highlights.summary: I thought making a will would be easy. Somehow, I ended up grilling my friends about their finances. I’ve spent a lot of my life thinking about death. When I was six, my dad had a heart attack.
body: Rather than feeling relief that his suffering was over and the purgatory of sickness was done, I turned to worrying incessantly about the health of my mother. Because my parents were immigrants, they had no family in Britain – no one they could ask to watch us for a couple of hours without payment, let alone look out for us after they were gone. So, just before I started secondary school, my mum asked one of my friends’ parents if she could name them as our next of kin. They said yes, but not wanting to rely on others, she continued to work hard to ensure we, as well as her family in Iraq, would have as much financial security as possible.

highlights.title: Building on Nemotron 3.5 Parse: Open Data, Fine-Tuning, and Faster Inference
highlights.summary: A Blog post by NVIDIA on Hugging Face
body: We recently released NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Parse, a compact document model that turns page images into structured data for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agents.

Now we’re building on that release with synthetic training datasets, a fine-tuning recipe, and a DFlash2 speculator for faster inference. We’re also sharing how we trained Parse 3.5: first teaching document understanding through supervised fine-tuning, then using reinforcement learning to improve accuracy, consistency, and reliable completion.

Parse extracts content from pages of documents into reading order, assigns content classes such as headings, paragraphs, tables, and charts, and returns bounding boxes that locate the content. Tables and charts become structured records that can power downstream document processing applications.
Figure 1. Actual model output from a synthetic operations brief, showing the connection between the page and its structured representation.

highlights.title: ‘South Park’ Season Finale Drops Kenny Into ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ as South America Comes Clean
highlights.summary: Power outages, penis billionaires and an undead Kenny collide as the season ties up (most of) its loose ends.
body: All is not well in South America (née South Park ) in the season 29 finale. The long-anticipated November release of Grand Theft Auto VI — the show’s metaphorical stand-in for the midterm elections — has finally arrived, but rolling power outages caused by local billionaires’ AI-powered data centers are keeping the townspeople — from the little-seen Goth Kids to Mr. Garrison to Big Gay Al, and of course, our core boy heroes — from enjoying the biggest media release of all time.

For an episode that packs plenty in, calling back to much of the season’s action and picking up most of the plot threads it introduced (minus, unfortunately, the great Tweek and Craig ), it’s Lu Kim, the Asian American owner of City Wok and now City Ending massage, who walks away with the heaviest storyline. He’s quickly scapegoated and placed under suspicious watch by armed South America residents, who are made aware of a Chinese spy that feels a little like a recent international tech world scandal. A Shitty Ending feels inevitable.

highlights.title: The bleph lady: Britain’s backstreet cosmetic surgeon
highlights.summary: Luyen Vu’s discount eye surgeries represent the dangers of an unregulated beauty industry. But for her fans, she is a folk hero. Robert Laycock, a facial plastic surgeon at Aintree University Hospital in Liverpool, first knew that something was up when a patient came to him in early 2024.
body: It is not unusual for botched private cosmetic surgeries to be fixed on the NHS. Laycock estimates that he sees three or four patients a year who need surgical intervention after too much tissue has been removed in a blepharoplasty. But something was different about this woman. “The surgery was done in a very odd way,” Laycock told me. The incision, he explained, had been made just beneath the eyebrow rather than on the crease of the eyelid. “[It’s] not the way that we would generally do a blepharoplasty in the UK.” He asked the woman where she’d had the work done but she was evasive and he dropped the subject.

highlights.title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
highlights.summary: In an announcement on Wednesday, the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company's "Starmind" initiative.
body: SpaceX aims to power AI capabilities here on Earth with its ‘Starmind’ constellation.

The FCC’s approval requires SpaceX to deploy at least one satellite by 2033, and meet the 1 million satellite milestone by 2040. The FCC also deferred SpaceX’s request to dispose of satellites located above 600km in space “graveyard” orbits, rather than having them burn up in the Earth’s atmosphere, saying the company hasn’t provided “sufficient information” about its disposal process plans.

SpaceX has described its Starmind project as a way to “capture solar energy in space to power” AI capabilities on Earth. The company says Starmind will transmit data to Earth using high-speed lasers that connect to Starlink. It plans to produce chips for its satellites at an upcoming Terafab facility.

Google has already taken its first steps toward putting compute into space, with the launch of a “Project Suncatcher” AI server satellite last month. Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin will carry out the first dedicated heavy-lift launch for Project Suncatcher in 2029.

highlights.summary: Stipe Miocic is widely regarded as the greatest heavyweight in UFC history. The former two-time champion holds several divisional records, including the most consecutive title defenses (3), total title defenses (4), and fight-night bonuses (9).
body: With a professional record of 20-5, the Croatian-American retired following his loss to Jon Jones at UFC 309 at Madison Square Garden. Although he was already 42 at the time, Miocic has not completely ruled out a return to the Octagon. However, the former champion has made it clear that any comeback would need to come with a significant financial incentive.

In a recent interview with Casino.org, Miocic opened up about the possibility of ending his retirement and said, “A lot of money. I guess there’s always a chance of coming out of retirement. Never say never. I’d probably fight anyone. I’ve never really cared about who I fought, so there’s no dream fight. But if there’s a lot of money involved, then I would definitely do it.”

Miocic boasts one of the most impressive resumes in heavyweight history, having shared the Octagon with the likes of Daniel Cormier, Jon Jones, Francis Ngannou, Alistair Overeem, and Junior dos Santos. Having faced and defeated several generations of heavyweight contenders, the former champion has accomplished virtually everything possible in the sport.

highlights.title: S&P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance and ‘key man’ risks
highlights.summary: The credit rating agency may lower Nvidia's credit rating to AA-, the fourth-highest rating.
body: S&P Global Ratings, one of the three major credit rating agencies, is considering downgrading Nvidia’s rating, citing concerns about the company’s management and governance practices.

Despite Nvidia’s strong financial performance, the ouster and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang has raised concerns about “weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning” and “key man risk,” meaning heavy reliance on Huang for its future success, S&P said in a statement.
The agency expects to finish its review within 90 days and could cut Nvidia’s rating from AA to AA-, the fourth-highest on its scale.

Although Nvidia is certain to keep its investment-grade rating, a downgrade could raise its borrowing costs. Because Nvidia backstops neoclouds and other infrastructure companies that lack strong credit on their own, a lower rating could make their debt costlier or force them to post more collateral.

highlights.title: Naomi Watts and Maude’s Éva Goicochea on Modernizing Sexual Wellness
highlights.summary: Long overlooked, women’s personal care categories ranging from menopause to sexual health are getting a rebrand from founders in the space who wanted to approach things differently.
body: It’s 2026, and women’s sex drives are still taboo. A crop of modern brands want to change that, with better products, more education and packaging you want sitting on your bedside table.

Naomi Watts founded her brand, Stripes Beauty, after starting menopause at 36. She found her typical products no longer worked, and that she didn’t understand how to navigate this stage of life — unexpectedly early — because she never had conversations about it with her mother. Maude founder Éva Goicochea started her brand with a vision to bring more access and smarter design to products once relegated to hush-hush purchasing.

At the Vogue Business Global Summit: New York, Watts and Goicochea sat down to discuss their experiences in creating brands for themselves first, what progress has been made in opening up access to women’s sexual health, and why getting older doesn’t mean that women should have to give up on their sex lives. This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.
Vogue: We’re here to talk about women’s sexual health. How did you both end up in this space?

highlights.title: Amazon is reportedly in talks to end Muse AI shopping block
highlights.summary: Amazon has held talks about letting Meta's Muse AI agent shop on its online marketplace, according to a report from Fortune. The discussions, which could end Amazon's block on Muse, reportedly center on the kinds of products the AI agent recommends and the potential impact on the ecommerce giant's…
body: Amazon is concerned that Muse AI could have an impact on its advertising revenue, according to Fortune.

As reported by Fortune, Amazon is concerned that it could lose advertising revenue by allowing Muse on its site, since it depends on actual humans seeing ads across its online marketplace. It’s also reportedly worried about the quality of the product search results that Muse will present to users, as well as whether the AI agent will affect Amazon’s relationship with customers. Neither Amazon nor Meta immediately responded to The Verge ’s request for comment.

Though some online retailers, such as Walmart, Best Buy, Gap, and Sephora, have opened their digital doors to AI agents like Muse, Amazon has been more hesitant. Amazon also blocked Perplexity’s AI agent from shopping on its site, and has instead focused on promoting its own Alexa for Shopping assistant, which customers can now text to shop on their behalf.

In the current holiday preamble, shoppers are seeking out pre-loved luxury, and hopeful recipients are adding resale finds to their wishlists. While aspirational consumers seek more bang for their buck, top-end consumers favor one-of-a-kind pieces with a story to tell.

According to Rati Sahi Levesque, The RealReal CEO, gift shoppers are spending big and small this holiday season: designer accessories under $250 and collectible pieces over $10,000. “One of the things I love about resale is that great taste isn’t confined to a particular price point,” she says, explaining that shoppers can do more with less, or invest in something extraordinary for their recipient. “Resale gives you access to things that money alone can’t buy in the primary market.”
